original:
{
  id: "concepts.books",
  title: "Books gains annotations and prices",
  question: "Where do activity's annotations and the Chainlink price sync go?",
  options: [
    { label: "books", text: "Both in books: an annotation gives a row its account, which is a book fact; prices value book facts." },
    { label: "activity", text: "Annotations stay in activity, which then writes books' facts or is read by books." },
  ],
  chosen: "books",
  why:
    "The frozen text says a fact is 'a change to the chart, an account given to a row, or a money event'. If activity " +
    "owned the annotation, either activity writes a book fact (a cross-concept write that is no money fact) or books reads " +
    "activity while activity reads books' chart: a loop. In books, `activity annotate` is one transaction. Prices were " +
    "already `bookPrices`; the Chainlink sync is its writer (P3 keeps it).",
  source: by("apps/docs/factory/operations/org.books.facts.list.yaml, activity.annotate.yaml; packages/backend/src/books/README.md:3"),
  affects: [f.concept_books, f.concept_activity, x.integration_chainlink],
}

{
  id: "concepts.books-token-scan",
  title: "Books scans the tokens an Organization adds; indexing has no workflow",
  question: "P3 keeps the scan of tokens added at run time. Which concept owns it, given that only books knows which tokens were added?",
  options: [
    { label: "books", text: "Books: one cron scans each added asset's Transfers to and from the company Safe from the block it was added, and writes book facts." },
    { label: "indexing", text: "Indexing, triggered by books' asset transition." },
    { label: "indexing-procedure", text: "Indexing owns a watched-token table that books writes through a procedure." },
  ],
  chosen: "books",
  why:
    "The frozen text says the books 'record its transfers' and 'Capxul starts scanning its transfers from the current " +
    "block'; its facts carry the token's symbol and no USD. The scan's only reader is books, and its list of tokens is " +
    "books' own `assets`. In indexing, the scan would have to follow books' transition, which needs indexing above books, " +
    "a cycle; a watched-token procedure is not one money fact. In books it reads its own table and the chain (chain-rpc " +
    "`getLogs`), and `org books assets remove` stops it. Indexing is then Ponder's views only.",
  source: reviewed("org.books.assets.add.yaml, org.books.assets.remove.yaml; P3 (scan added tokens); platform/jobs.ts:125-139"),
  affects: [f.concept_books, f.concept_indexing, x.integration_chain_rpc],
}

{
  id: "concepts.budgets",
  title: "New concept: budgets, from allowances, departments and ceilings",
  question: "Where do spending allowances, departments and payout ceilings live under v4?",
  options: [
    { label: "budgets", text: "One budgets concept: allowances and departments are both v4 budgets, with office hats and ceilings." },
    { label: "split", text: "Allowances in permissions and departments in payroll, as the old code had them." },
  ],
  chosen: "budgets",
  why:
    "The designed text says it directly: 'A spending allowance becomes a small budget under a hat the member wears', and a " +
    "department is a top or child budget. Both are one v4 contract (Budgets), one tree and one authority rule (the wearer " +
    "of the budget's hat or of any above it). Keeping them apart would duplicate the tree and its authority check.",
  source: by("apps/docs/factory/operations/org.allowance.create.yaml, org.department.create.yaml (designed)"),
  affects: [f.concept_budgets],
}

{
  id: "concepts.contacts",
  title: "New concept: contacts, split from parties",
  question: "Where does the address book live?",
  options: [
    { label: "contacts", text: "A small contacts concept above organizations." },
    { label: "parties", text: "Keep contacts in parties and let the runtime check Organization membership." },
    { label: "payments", text: "Put contacts in payments, as their area suggests." },
  ],
  chosen: "contacts",
  why:
    "An Organization's address book is acted on by its members, which only a concept above organizations can check; " +
    "parties must stay below organizations because an Organization registers its Party at birth. A hidden runtime check " +
    "would be a dependency the book cannot see. In payments, banking (bank accounts on a contact) would still have to " +
    "reach into payments for a non-money record.",
  source: by("apps/docs/factory/operations/contact.add.yaml ('a member of the Organization for its book')"),
  affects: [f.concept_contacts, f.concept_parties, f.concept_banking],
}

{
  id: "concepts.documents",
  title: "Documents stays, below everything that stamps a document hash",
  question: "Where does documents sit, and how does it know who may read a document?",
  options: [
    { label: "below-money", text: "Below payments, requests and payroll; participants are given when the document is stored." },
    { label: "as-is", text: "Keep documents reading payments, requests and books to find a document's participants." },
  ],
  chosen: "below-money",
  why:
    "A document is born with its subject (K2: a command, its Payments and their documents are born together), so the " +
    "subject's concept stores it through a procedure and must depend on documents. Documents then cannot read its subjects; " +
    "giving it the participants at store time means it never has to.",
  source: by("K2 in docs/as-is/payments.md; docs/as-is/archive/shared/foundation.ts (documents imports 7 concepts)"),
  affects: [f.concept_documents, f.concept_payments, f.concept_requests],
}

{
  id: "concepts.line-budgets",
  title: "No line budgets on concepts yet",
  question: "Should the concept records carry `lines` budgets now?",
  options: [
    { label: "later", text: "Leave `lines` unset; each concept's design sets its budget from its own records." },
    { label: "now", text: "Set budgets now from the old lines less the plumbing." },
  ],
  chosen: "later",
  why:
    "A line budget is only as good as the design under it, and the per-concept designs have not been written. The old " +
    "lines are mostly plumbing (about two thirds of an area is ceremony, and 166 files are emit, intent, load or record), " +
    "so they would anchor the numbers on the system being replaced, the same objection P5 made to per-operation budgets.",
  source: by("docs/mission/findings.md (two thirds ceremony); P3 (166 plumbing files); P5 option A"),
  affects: [...f.CONCEPTS],
}

{
  id: "concepts.map",
  title: "23 target concepts in one dependency order",
  question: "How many concepts, and in what order, so that every old responsibility lands once and nothing loops?",
  options: [
    { label: "keep-17", text: "Keep the 17 old concepts and cut the loop by moving imports." },
    {
      label: "23-dag",
      text:
        "23 concepts in this order: access, media, parties, indexing, approvals, accounts, organizations, board, agents, " +
        "projects, budgets, books, documents, contacts, payments, payroll, banking, requests, applications, equity, activity, " +
        "notices, devnet.",
    },
    { label: "fewer", text: "Merge into about 8 large concepts (identity, organizations, money, books, equity, devnet...)." },
  ],
  chosen: "23-dag",
  why:
    "15 of the 17 old concepts formed one import loop, and the loop ran through real responsibilities in the wrong place: " +
    "permissions inside organizations' authority, executions inside payments, Directors inside organizations, waitlist " +
    "credit inside access. v4 itself splits them: Budgets, Agreements, Hats and the Signer Gate, AgentOwner and the equity " +
    "clones are separate contracts with separate authority. Each target concept owns one of those nouns, and its " +
    "dependencies point only at concepts it must read or invoke. Merging into fewer concepts would break the line budgets " +
    "(`sys:loc`) and hide ownership (P4 option C's objection). The new ones are small and each has a decision below. " +
    "Projects, the 23rd, is new in the rebuild (aaron.projects): it sits after agents and below budgets, books, requests " +
    "and payroll, which read it (projects.dependencies).",
  source: by("docs/as-is/archive/shared/foundation.ts (108 edges, 15-concept cycle); docs/planning/protocol-v4/architecture.md; aaron.projects"),
  affects: [...f.CONCEPTS],
}

{
  id: "concepts.organizations",
  title: "Organizations keeps the workspace; Directors and equity leave",
  question: "What stays in organizations, the old 30k-line reference concept?",
  options: [
    { label: "workspace", text: "Identity, setup and install, the deployment record, members and invitations; Directors and proposals to board; equity and votes to equity." },
    { label: "as-is", text: "Keep everything, including directors, equity, rounds, proposals and votes." },
  ],
  chosen: "workspace",
  why:
    "Members and invitations are needed by almost every concept (who may act for this Organization), so they must sit low; " +
    "Board proposals are opened by budgets, payments, payroll, agents and equity, so the Board must sit above organizations " +
    "and below them. Keeping both in one concept is what tied organizations and permissions into a two-way loop (76 and 37 " +
    "imports). Equity is low priority and off the critical path, so it should not share a line budget with the workspace.",
  source: by("docs/mission/findings.md (organizations-permissions cycle); docs/spec/40-capxul-team.md (equity low priority)"),
  affects: [f.concept_organizations, f.concept_board, f.concept_activity],
}

{
  id: "concepts.parties",
  title: "Parties is the directory and absorbs profiles",
  question: "What does parties own, and where do profiles, contacts, verification and engagements go?",
  options: [
    { label: "directory", text: "Parties owns Parties, handles, Safes, owners, profiles and resolution; contacts, verification and engagements leave." },
    { label: "as-is", text: "Keep parties with contacts, verification and engagements, and keep profiles separate." },
  ],
  chosen: "directory",
  why:
    "A profile is a person's own Party seen by others: its display name is what a counterparty sees, so it belongs with the " +
    "Party (old profiles was one `identities` table linked to the person's Party). Contacts need an Organization's " +
    "membership, which sits above parties, so they move up (concepts.contacts). Verification is Bridge's KYC for bank rails " +
    "only, so it moves to banking. Engagements were what payroll runs paid; v4 Agreements replace them. What remains is " +
    "the one thing everyone below organizations needs: a name, the Safe it routes money to, and who owns that Safe.",
  source: by("packages/backend/src/profiles/README.md:3; apps/docs/factory/operations/verify.start.yaml; ADR-0022"),
  affects: [f.concept_parties, f.concept_contacts, f.concept_banking],
}

{
  id: "dependencies.activity-books",
  title: "Activity reads books; books never reads activity",
  question: "Old activity and books imported each other. Which way now?",
  options: [
    { label: "activity-up", text: "Activity reads books' annotations, chart and prices; books owns annotations." },
    { label: "books-up", text: "Books reads activity's annotations." },
  ],
  chosen: "activity-up",
  why: "Annotations moved to books (concepts.books), so activity is a pure reader above books and nothing reads activity.",
  source: by("docs/as-is/archive/shared/foundation.ts (activity imports books; books imports activity's neighbours)"),
  affects: [f.concept_activity, f.concept_books],
}

{
  id: "dependencies.books-below-money",
  title: "Books sits below payments and banking, which write its money facts",
  question: "Which way do books and payments point, and how is a settled Payment's book fact written?",
  options: [
    { label: "below", text: "Payments and banking depend on books and write a money fact's book fact through its procedure, in the same transaction." },
    { label: "consumer", text: "Books depends on payments and consumes `payment_transitioned` through the outbox." },
  ],
  chosen: "below",
  why:
    "ADR-0042 decision 1 (accepted) and P4 put a book fact in the caller's transaction so a fact is never lost or doubled, " +
    "and K10 says a settled Payment always has its book facts. Books needs nothing from payments: its facts carry what they " +
    "record. The old code had the door (`recordSettledPaymentInTx`) and never used it; the target imports only the door.",
  source: by("ADR-0042 decision 1; P4; docs/as-is/payments.md (K10, 0 door imports)"),
  affects: [f.concept_books, f.concept_payments, f.concept_banking],
}

{
  id: "dependencies.books-payroll",
  title: "Payroll posts a run's accrual through books' door; books never reads payroll",
  question:
    "A run Capxul computed must credit Payroll Payable and the deductions' liabilities when it is submitted, and take " +
    "them back when it is cancelled (books.payroll-accrual). Which way does the edge between books and payroll point?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "payroll-up",
      text:
        "Payroll depends on books and invokes `books.record-payroll-accrual` in `payroll.runs.submit` and " +
        "`payroll.runs.cancel`, in their own transactions; books reads nothing of payroll's.",
    },
    { label: "books-up", text: "Books depends on payroll and follows `payroll_entry_transitioned` to post the accrual." },
  ],
  chosen: "payroll-up",
  why:
    "Books sits below payments (dependencies.books-below-money) and payroll above payments " +
    "(dependencies.payments-payroll), so books depending on payroll would make a cycle through payments. The accrual " +
    "and the submitted run are one money fact: a run that owes its people must have the liability in the books, or a " +
    "slip's Payment is booked against a payable nothing credited, so the door runs in the run's transaction (P4), as " +
    "payments and banking write their book facts. Books needs no new edge for it: the lines name books' own accounts and " +
    "an Employee's Party id, which books keeps as given.",
  source: by("books.payroll-accrual, payroll.accrual (blueprint/payroll/decisions.ts); docs/design/frappe/accounting.md (For other lanes: payroll); P4"),
  affects: [f.concept_books, f.concept_payments],
}

{
  id: "dependencies.payments-payroll",
  title: "Payroll depends on payments to pay a run; payments never depends on payroll",
  question: "Old payments called payroll's settle-run inside its settlement, and payroll built payments. Which way now?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "payroll-up",
      text:
        "Payroll depends on payments: a run's payment is born through `payments.prepare-command` (purpose payroll) and its " +
        "settlement follows `payment_transitioned`. Payments never depends on payroll; collections are born as Payments " +
        "from chain facts.",
    },
    { label: "independent", text: "The earlier choice: neither depends on the other; payroll depends on budgets, and collections are born from chain facts." },
    { label: "procedure", text: "Keep `payroll.settle-run` as a procedure payments invokes (P4's example)." },
  ],
  chosen: "payroll-up",
  why:
    "Rewritten to payroll.scope, which supersedes concepts.payroll: runs came back as Frappe HR's Payroll Entries and " +
    "Salary Slips. A run's payment is a Payment and its route is payments' (one request key per command, the funding " +
    "check, the claim escrow for a new hire, one settlement path with its reorg reversal), so payroll births it through " +
    "payments' door, as requests and banking do (payroll.pays-through-payments). A slip's paid state and its settled " +
    "transaction may lag a second, so they follow the Payment's transition (P4's outbox), never a procedure payments " +
    "invokes: P4 kept settle-run only because a settled Payment with its run still open was a money bug, and a slip " +
    "following the event closes that without payments knowing payroll. An agreement collection is still " +
    "`Agreements.collect`, whose PaymentSent payments settles like any other. The edge points down the order (payroll " +
    "after payments), so it makes no cycle, and payments never writes or reads payroll's tables.",
  source: by("payroll.scope, payroll.pays-through-payments; P4 (settle-run procedure); docs/as-is/payments.md (K11); docs/design/frappe/payroll.md"),
  affects: [f.concept_payments],
}

{
  id: "dependencies.board-below-proposers",
  title: "Every concept that needs the Board depends on board",
  question: "Budgets, payments, payroll, agents and equity all make Board batches. Which way do they point?",
  options: [
    { label: "proposers-up", text: "They depend on board and open a proposal in their own transaction; they follow `proposal_transitioned`." },
    { label: "board-up", text: "Board depends on them and builds their batches." },
  ],
  chosen: "proposers-up",
  why:
    "The concept that knows the intent (a department, a Board payment, an org-owned agent's freeze) builds the calls; the " +
    "Board only collects approvals and executes. If board built them it would depend on every money concept. A proposal " +
    "and the intent it carries are one fact (rules.procedures), so opening it is a procedure.",
  source: by("org.department.create.yaml, payment.send.yaml (--as-directors), agent.create.yaml (designed)"),
  affects: [f.concept_board, f.concept_budgets, f.concept_payments, f.concept_agents],
}

{
  id: "integrations.indexer",
  title: "The indexer is a service for what depends on Ponder's progress",
  question: "Ponder's tables are in the same Postgres. Why an integration at all, and what are its calls?",
  options: [
    { label: "progress-calls", text: "Plain indexed reads are table reads; head, awaitBlock and factsOf are calls, because Ponder may lag, reindex or be rebuilt." },
    { label: "tables-only", text: "No integration: everything is a table read." },
  ],
  chosen: "progress-calls",
  why:
    "A read that needs a fact Ponder has not indexed yet must wait for it or fail with a code, not answer with nothing " +
    "(the old system answered 'pending' forever when the indexer was down, old R2). Making those reads calls gives them a " +
    "timeout, a failure mapping and a `call.indexer.*` span (P6), so a lagging Ponder is visible in every trace that waits on it.",
  source: by("docs/as-is/payments.md (R2, settle treats an unavailable indexer as pending); P6"),
  affects: [x.integration_indexer, f.concept_indexing],
}

{
  id: "operations.contact-get-in-banking",
  title: "`contact get` is banking's flow, because it returns the contact's bank accounts",
  question: "`contact get` returns `bankAccounts`, which banking owns, and contacts sits below banking. Which concept owns it?",
  options: [
    { label: "banking", text: "Banking: its flow calls contacts' read of the entry, then its own masked accounts for that Party." },
    { label: "contacts", text: "Contacts, returning the entry without its bank accounts." },
    { label: "contacts-up", text: "Contacts above banking (banking would lose the contact a saved account belongs to: a cycle)." },
  ],
  chosen: "banking",
  why:
    "The frozen `returns` names `bankAccounts` (P10 rung 1), and the old CLI made a second call for them. A flow composes " +
    "only concepts its concept depends on, and banking is the one concept above contacts that owns the accounts, as " +
    "`contact bank add` already is. The contacts designer found this and kept the record in contacts until the map moved " +
    "it (contacts.get-bank-accounts); the entry's rpc stays contacts' for banking's flow to call.",
  source: adversarial("contact.get.yaml (returns: bankAccounts); blueprint/contacts/decisions.ts (contacts.get-bank-accounts)"),
  affects: [f.concept_banking, f.concept_contacts],
}

{
  id: "operations.owners",
  title: "Each frozen operation has one owning concept; an area spreads over several",
  question: "Which concept designs each of the 215 frozen operations?",
  options: [
    { label: "by-area-with-exceptions", text: "Each area maps to a concept; an operation whose behaviour belongs to another concept goes there (OPERATION_OWNERS)." },
    { label: "by-area", text: "Every operation stays with its area's concept." },
  ],
  chosen: "by-area-with-exceptions",
  why:
    "Areas are how people find commands, not concepts (the operation record says so). 134 operations sit in their area's " +
    "primary concept (AREA_CONCEPTS) and 81 move with their behaviour: agents, session and local commands out of accounts; " +
    "`doctor` and keys to applications; verification and `contact bank add` to banking; invitations and members to " +
    "organizations, `invite accept` to banking, allowances and `org member invite` to budgets and votes to equity out of " +
    "governance; requests, services, the inbox, contacts, documents, `address` and `balance` out of payments, with " +
    "`contact get` to banking; `activity annotate` to books; `bank match` to requests; `org department pay` to payments; " +
    "`dev fund` to accounts, `dev key` to applications. The map is typed against every frozen id, so none can be missed, " +
    "and every concept but media, parties, indexing, approvals and notices owns at least one operation. The rule behind " +
    "each exception: an operation's flow sits in a concept that depends on every concept whose rpcs it composes " +
    "(operations.sign-in-in-accounts, operations.member-invite-in-budgets, operations.invite-accept-in-banking, " +
    "operations.contact-get-in-banking); every devnet-only operation is devnet's (operations.dev-mail-notices-in-devnet).",
  source: by("blueprint/baseline/operations.ts (215 operations, 11 areas); OPERATION_OWNERS in blueprint/shared/foundation.ts"),
  affects: [...f.CONCEPTS],
}

{
  id: "responsibilities.keepers",
  title: "'Manage books' is the Books officer hat",
  question: "Old books listed its keepers (who holds Manage books). What is that on v4?",
  options: [
    { label: "hat", text: "The wearers of the Books hat: board grants and revokes it, books reads its wearers from indexing." },
    { label: "table", text: "Keep a keepers table in books." },
  ],
  chosen: "hat",
  why: "On v4 every officer permission is a hat granted by a Board batch (CAP-1101), and Capxul reads it only from Hats; a table would copy the chain.",
  source: reviewed("org.member.grant.yaml (designed: Books, Invoicing and People hats); packages/backend/src/books/keepers/"),
  affects: [f.concept_books, f.concept_board],
}

{
  id: "responsibilities.landings",
  title: "Every old concept area lands in a target concept, or is dropped by a decision",
  question: "How is it shown that every responsibility of the 17 old concepts lands somewhere?",
  options: [
    { label: "typed-map", text: "OLD_AREAS in shared/landings.ts: each of the old concepts' area folders, the target concepts it lands in, and the decision that put it there." },
    { label: "prose", text: "Each target concept's `about` names what it absorbs." },
  ],
  chosen: "typed-map",
  why:
    "A concept's `about` says what it absorbs, but nothing checks that the old list is covered. The map lists all 91 " +
    "area folders under packages/backend/src/<concept>/, plus the root files of documents and parties, and every entry names a " +
    "decision record, so a dropped responsibility is a judgment a reviewer can find. The map is not a record: the build " +
    "follows its decisions' `affects`.",
  source: reviewed("ls packages/backend/src/<concept>/ at 0d2be303e"),
  affects: [...f.CONCEPTS],
}

{
  id: "rules.fde-acts-for-asker",
  title: "Every tenant guard resolves the hosted FDE to its open ask's asker, or refuses",
  question:
    "The eighth batch's ruling that anyone may ask the hosted FDE, which does for them only what their own hats allow, " +
    "is applied in organizations (organizations.fde-for-the-asker). Every concept's rpcs authorise a caller through " +
    "organizations' tenant guard. How does that guard, and the Core SDK, treat a call the hosted FDE makes?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "asker-or-nothing",
      text:
        "A hosted FDE call carries the act-for token its turn's ask minted (the FDE host passes it as an egress header). " +
        "The tenant guard every concept runs (organizations' MEMBER_GUARD and the guards built on it) resolves such a " +
        "call to the open ask's asker by the token's hash (`org-fde-asks.by_token`): their Seat and hats for a member, " +
        "their Party alone for a guest; the call is the asker's, logged with the ask. An expired, ended or unknown " +
        "token, or none, is ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED: the hosted FDE never resolves to its own Seat, so only a self-run " +
        "own agent (`agent create --org`) acts as itself. Under such a session the Core SDK's signing steps hand the " +
        "approval over to the asker (the `--no-wait` hand-over, or `--json` for the payment family) instead of signing. " +
        "An rpc behind a preview (G5: `contact link`, `org hr employee leave`, `org head connect|disconnect`, `org head " +
        "doc remove`, `org hr advance settle`, the CRM's sends and WhatsApp connect and disconnect) refuses an act-for call " +
        "ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED, since the preview is the asker's own to answer.",
    },
    { label: "own-seat", text: "The FDE calls as its own Seat, with hats the Board grants it, whoever asked." },
  ],
  chosen: "asker-or-nothing",
  why:
    "Resolving the call in the one guard every concept already runs applies the ruling everywhere at once, with no " +
    "concept checking two Seats; refusing a call with no live token keeps an FDE that nobody asked from acting at all, " +
    "and refusing a preview's rpc keeps the asker's own answer theirs. Handing over instead of signing keeps every " +
    "signature the asker's Safe's, as authority.md requires. Its own Seat with granted hats would let anyone who may ask " +
    "act with hats they do not wear. organizations.fde-for-the-asker is the concept's record of the same choice; this " +
    "states it for every concept's guard.",
  source: "Claude, world pass build, 9 November 2026; under aaron.fde-anyone; evidence: organizations.fde-for-the-asker; blueprint/organizations/apps.ts (MEMBER_GUARD); docs/design/new-commands.md (G4, G5)",
  affects: [
    f.concept_organizations, f.concept_agents, f.concept_contacts, f.concept_payments,
    f.concept_budgets, f.component_core_sdk, x.integration_fde_host,
  ],
}

{
  id: "rules.new-operations",
  title: "A new operation is booked with a decision citing an Aaron ruling, and a claim",
  question:
    "system.frozen-behaviour keeps the 215 operations as the list of capabilities, and packages/blueprint-engine/scripts/check-frozen.ts refused any " +
    "target operation that is none of them. Aaron has since ruled new capabilities fundamental: every Organization starts " +
    "with a CRM and Projects in Frappe's shapes, and its payroll is Frappe HR's (aaron.frappe-shape, " +
    "aaron.crm-frappe-shape, aaron.projects), and aaron.projects says their operations are new capabilities, designed " +
    "book first with a decision pack. So the lanes booked those rpcs behind SDK-only flows (contacts.crm-capabilities, " +
    "payroll.hr-surface) or not at all (projects.commands, organizations.commands): no CLI command could be booked. On " +
    "what terms may the target book an operation that is none of the 215?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "cited-ruling",
      text:
        "A new operation is booked only when: (1) a decision on it other than this rule (its `affects` lists the " +

{
  id: "tooling.hooks",
  title: "Hooks: staged fmt, lint and secrets; pre-push runs every gate on the tree",
  question: "What do pre-commit and pre-push run, within what time, and which lessons of the old hooks do they keep?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "two-scripts",
      text:
        "pre-commit: CI=1 vp staged (fmt and lint on staged files, gitleaks on the staged diff), at most 5 s for 30 files. " +
        "pre-push: refuse any update or deletion of main or integration/build and a ref that is not HEAD, then vp fmt " +
        "--check, vp lint, " +
        "tsc -b, generate:check, pnpm book and vp test run on the whole tree, at most 90 s until B3.",
    },
    { label: "staged-only", text: "Only the staged checks; leave everything else to CI." },
    { label: "scoped", text: "Scope pre-push to the files the push changes, as the old check.sh did." },
  ],
  chosen: "two-scripts",
  why:
    "The old hooks recorded the lessons: every vp call needs CI=1 (vp opened /dev/tty and a pre-push 'hung' for nine " +
    "minutes); a pushed ref that is not HEAD must be refused because gates read the working tree; vp staged appends paths, " +
    "so tsc cannot run there; no --fix at commit, because the Effect fixes rewrite code; hooks call direct verbs, never the " +
    "task graph, after vp was SIGKILLed in a macOS worktree. Staged-only lets a red tree reach the remote and costs a CI " +
    "round trip per mistake. Scoping by changed files took a 100-line script; the whole tree fits 90 s now (book checks " +
    "about 15 s, lint and types seconds), and scoping is the first remedy when it stops fitting. The old pre-push ran no tsc " +
    "and no tests because the SDK's declaration emit hit a memory cliff; every target project is noEmit. Measured through " +
    "the dispatcher with a bare remote: pushes to main and integration/build, a deletion of main and a ref that is not " +
    "HEAD were refused; a first draft that skipped deletions before checking the protected names let the deletion through, " +
    "which the old merge gate refused.",
  source: by("/home/user/factory/lefthook.yml and .lefthook/pre-push/check.sh; /home/user/factory/vite.config.ts staged block; prototype hook timings"),
  affects: [f.system_capxul],
}

{
  id: "time.chain-judged-deadlines",
  title: "Chain time is a block's fact; the chain's head judges a deadline it enforces",
  question:
    "On staging the chain is Base Sepolia, whose blocks carry the sequencer's time. Payroll's, equity's and approvals' " +
    "timers act on deadlines a contract or the EntryPoint enforces with block.timestamp. How do they meet the one clock?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "head-judges",
      text:
        "Chain time is read, never computed: a fact's time is its block's timestamp (indexing's rows, chain-rpc.getBlock). " +
        "A time that reaches the chain (a validUntil, a cliff, a period's start, a vote's end, a close) is a whole second. " +
        "A timer for a deadline the chain enforces is due at the first second at which the chain's own rule gives the new " +
        "answer, read off the contract: v4 Agreements' offer expiry and Budgets' payAt change at the deadline second " +
        "itself (`>=`), while OpenZeppelin's Governor keeps a vote Active through its deadline second, so a vote's end is " +
        "due at voteEnd + 1; the EntryPoint's validAfter bound is read off the pinned EntryPoint the same way. When the " +
        "timer fires it checks the head: while the head has not reached the due second (on staging it trails now), it " +
        "re-arms for the shortfall instead of acting or failing, and it acts once Ponder has indexed that head, so a fact " +
        "mined before the deadline (an accept in the deadline's last second) is seen before a lapse is decided. A span of " +
        "chain-dated facts (a month's books, a budget period) is half-open, [start, end), as the v4 Calendar's periods " +
        "are, and a process that closes one waits the same way until the head and Ponder are past its end. On a devnet " +
        "the head is at now at every settled stop (devnet.only-miner), so with due seconds set by this rule the re-arm " +
        "never happens there.",
    },
    { label: "trust-now", text: "Act at now and treat an early revert as a failure." },
  ],
  chosen: "head-judges",
  why:
    "On staging now and the head's time are close but not equal: the head trails by up to a block and a host's clock can " +
    "run ahead of the sequencer's. The chain's judgment is final, so the decision that depends on it defers to it; a " +
    "failure for a second's difference would be a defect the devnet could never show. The re-arm alone is not enough: " +
    "a lapse needs no chain call, so nothing reverts to say it is early, and a payee's accept can land in a block dated " +
    "before the expiry after the backend has lapsed the offer. And the devnet's equality of head and now hides an " +
    "off-by-one, not removes it: a timer due at voteEnd fires at a stop whose block is at voteEnd, where Governor.state " +
    "still answers Active. Revised by the time review, 8 November 2026.",
  source: by("v4 src/money/Agreements.sol:198 (>= offerExpiresAt), Budgets.sol:288 (< payAt); OZ GovernorUpgradeable.state; blueprint/equity/processes.ts:403"),
  affects: [
    f.component_backend, f.component_chain, x.integration_chain_rpc, x.integration_indexer, 
    f.concept_approvals, f.concept_books, f.concept_budgets,
  ],
}

{
  id: "time.drift-watch",
  title: "Staging watches the chain's lag behind now and each host's skew",
  question: "On staging and production nothing makes the chain's time and the backend's now equal. How is drift seen before it becomes a defect?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "two-signals",
      text:
        "Every read of the chain head (chain-rpc.getBlock, the indexer's head) records `time.chain_lag_ms`, now minus the " +
        "head's timestamp, on its span; each transaction records `time.db_skew_ms`, the backend's now minus Postgres' " +
        "clock_timestamp(), read in the round trip that sets the tenant. B5 adds live evals and alerts: chain lag outside " +
        "-2 s to +60 s for five minutes, and a host's skew beyond one second.",
    },
    { label: "none", text: "Trust NTP and the sequencer." },
  ],
  chosen: "two-signals",
  why:
    "A negative lag means the backend's clock is behind the chain's, so a deadline the chain enforces can pass before " +
    "Capxul acts; a large positive one means a stale node or a stalled head. Several backend instances share one " +
    "Postgres, so its clock is the reference that shows one host's skew, which would reorder rows and fire timers early " +
    "or late. Both ride on reads already made, so the watch costs no new call.",
  source: by("blueprint/shared/external.ts (chain-rpc.getBlock, indexer.head); blueprint/shared/foundation.ts (staging: two or more backend instances)"),
  affects: [f.environment_staging, f.component_backend, f.component_postgres, x.integration_chain_rpc, x.integration_indexer],
}

{
  id: "time.world-channels",
  title: "Every outside channel belongs to its world and follows its clock",
  question:
    "aaron.world-clock: emails, WhatsApp, the Frappe head and the FDE follow the world's clock, and a world's outside " +
    "channels are its own (a devnet's mail goes to its sink, WhatsApp to a stand-in, a connected head follows the " +
    "clock). Which channels does each world hold, and how does each stay inside it?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "world-owns-channels",
      text:
        "A channel is a stand-in inside the world that follows its clock, or, on staging, the real service held to the " +
        "world's own parties. Mail: on a devnet and a shared world the sink, so none leaves, a shared world's joiner " +
        "reading only its own mailboxes; on staging Resend, but only to the mailboxes MAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS lists " +
        "(domains and addresses), a send to any other address refused before Resend as Resend refuses a recipient " +
        "(INVALID_INPUT), so the notice records the failure. A head's own email (ERPNext's and Frappe HR's notifications) " +
        "goes the same way: to the sink on a devnet and a shared world, and on staging only to those mailboxes, " +
        "through the Capxul app's mail hook. WhatsApp: a stand-in of Meta's Cloud API on a devnet and a shared world; " +
        "on staging only a Meta test number, which sends only to the recipients registered with it, so staging's " +
        "connect admits no other number. The Frappe head: a follower of the world's clock on a devnet and a shared " +
        "world, through the Capxul app's hooks; on staging a site on its host's clock. The FDE host: the stand-in on a devnet, the world's own namespace following " +
        "its clock in a shared world, the host's clock on staging. Bridge, the bundler and paymaster, Chainlink and " +
        "PostHog: the stand-ins and fakes already follow; Bridge's sandbox, which a banking eval may use on a devnet, " +
        "does not, so such an eval never relies on Bridge's own times, and a shared world uses only the stand-in. Every message is dated at the world's now; a vendor's envelope " +
        "stays real (time.real-elapsed). Production's channels are the real ones. A season's reset restores every " +
        "channel's state with its world (time.seasons). The devnet's decisions say how: devnet.season-players, " +
        "devnet.whatsapp-stand-in, devnet.site-follows-world, devnet.fde-host-follows-world, devnet.stand-ins-follow and " +
        "devnet.stateful-followers.",
    },
    { label: "real-channels", text: "Send a world's mail and messages through the real services, dated by the world's clock." },
  ],
  chosen: "world-owns-channels",
  why:
    "A world's story is one story only if what it says to people happens inside it: an email dated next March from a " +
    "world at rate 4, sent to a real inbox, is a false message in the real world, and a code that went to a real inbox " +
    "could not be read by the eval that needs it. Holding each channel in its world keeps every date in it on one clock " +
    "and every party one of its own. Staging cannot keep Resend or Meta in a sink without ceasing to test them, so it " +
    "holds their recipients instead; Meta's own test number already sends only to registered recipients. For the owners " +
    "of the mail, frappe-head and fde-host integrations, and of the WhatsApp integration the CRM books: each one's text " +
    "says how it stays in its world.",
  source: WORLD("aaron.world-clock; docs/decisions/open-for-aaron.md (the CRM tracks every conversation); blueprint/shared/external.ts (mail, frappe-head, fde-host)"),
  affects: [

    x.integration_chainlink, x.integration_posthog, f.environment_devnet, f.environment_staging, f.environment_shared_world,
    f.component_frappe_app,
  ],
}

{

    "which always refuse, beside `org board director` and `org board threshold`; `balance` in the verb place; G5's " +
    "`--from <budget>` against the 215's dated `--from`; and 67 HR DocTypes reached only through `org head doc`. Which " +
    "change?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "keep-and-say",
      text:
        "No spelling changes; the grammar and the help say what each is. G3's 'show <id> is not used' binds new commands, " +
        "and the 215's eleven agreement commands moved by their group word only, so `payroll agreement show` keeps the " +
        "215's verb. `org hr employee leave` keeps G3's lifecycle verb, Frappe's own (the Employee's status Left); the " +
        "noun before it (`employee`) tells it from the record `org hr leave`. `apply` keeps its two meanings, each " +
        "Frappe's word (Leave Application; frappe.model.workflow apply_workflow), and G3 says so. `balance` is a view " +
        "read by its noun, as the 215's `balance`, and G3 lists it. G5's `--from <budget>` binds new commands; the " +
        "215's `dev prices set --from <date>` and `org payroll agreement change --from <date>` keep theirs. `capxul " +
        "--help` marks `org director add|remove|replace|threshold` retired, naming `org board director` and `org board " +

        "for HR's other DocTypes (recruitment, appraisal, training).",

{
  id: "surface.tree",
  title: "One command tree: scope, then the group, then the record, then the verb",
  question:
    "Aaron, 9 November 2026, on question 48: 'The number was not the issue. We need everything you can do on Frappe to " +
    "be programmatic and accessible from our tooling. It's the logical groupings.' The 380 commands start with 79 " +
    "different words (each `org` noun counted as one), and HR alone is spread over twelve of them. How is the surface " +
    "grouped?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "groups",
      text:
        "Every command reads `[org] <group or noun> [<noun>] <verb>`, never more than four words before its arguments. " +
        "`org` stays the scope, as in the 215: it begins every command only an Organization has, acting for the " +
        "Organization `--org` or `use org` names; a command without it acts as yourself, or for whoever you act as. The " +
        "surface has thirteen logical groups (SURFACE_GROUPS). Where a Frappe app holds the records, the group is a word, " +
        "the app's: `org hr`, `org payroll`, `org crm`, `org projects` and `org head` (the Frappe site), beside the 215's " +
        "`org books`; where a person has their own side of it, the same word without `org`: `hr`, `payroll`. Capxul's " +
        "native areas (who you are and sign-in, the CLI and your apps, your money, the Organization and its people and " +
        "departments, governance and equity, agents and the FDE, the devnet) keep the 215's nouns, which already say what " +
        "they are, and are grouped as sections of `capxul --help` and of the reference. Under a group, a record is its " +
        "DocType's noun and every verb is G3's. 119 commands move: 108 of the 165 new ones, and the 215's eleven " +
        "agreement commands into payroll (surface.payroll-group).",
    },
    { label: "flat-sections", text: "Keep every command where it is, and group them only in `--help` and the reference." },
    {
      label: "words-everywhere",
      text:
        "Make every area a word as well: `org equity round create`, `org governance proposal approve`, `money payment " +
        "send`. Most of the 215 move.",
    },
    {
      label: "domain-first",
      text:
        "Drop `org` and start every command with its group, the Organization chosen by `use org`: `hr leave approve`. A " +
        "list could not say whether it is yours or the Organization's, and about 150 of the 215 move.",

  chosen: "groups",
  why:
    "The scatter Aaron names is where a Frappe app's records sat as loose nouns beside unrelated ones: HR's twelve, " +
    "projects' five, the head's four, payroll's payslips apart from its runs. A Frappe user looks for them by app, as " +

    "`advance`). No command is longer than the 215's longest (`org books accounts add`). The SDK follows the words " +

    "Aaron, 10 November 2026, on the portal's Questions page: accepted as recommended. What it now applies to: of the tree's 394 rows, 159 are still booked (the native groups: identity, builders, " +
    "money, the Organization, governance's board, agents, the devnet and the eleven pay agreements under payroll). The HR, projects and head " +
    "groups and most of the books, payroll and CRM rows left the built book with the cut and are Frappe's, reached through the door " +

{
  id: "parties.frappe-identity",
  title: "The directory is the identity half of Frappe CRM's Contact and Organization",
  question:
    "The directory of people and companies is to be a global CRM in Frappe CRM's shape. Frappe CRM keeps a person as a " +
    "Contact and a company as a CRM Organization, one site per business, each holding that business's own knowledge " +
    "(mailboxes, phones, titles, territories, revenue, deals). What does the global directory hold, and how does a " +
    "Frappe record meet it?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "identity-half",
      text:
        "Each Party is the global identity a Frappe Contact (kind person, agent or address) or CRM Organization (kind " +
        "organization) stands for: its name (`display_name`, which Contact's `full_name` or CRM Organization's " +
        "`organization_name` shows when the owner's book gives no label of its own), its picture (`photo_file_id`: " +
        "`image`, `organization_logo`) and the key Frappe itself " +
        "dedupes a person by, the mailbox (`mailbox_digest`). Everything else those doctypes hold is the owner's, in its " +
        "book (contacts), in the same doctypes' fields. A connected head carries `party_id` as one Custom Field on " +
        "Contact, CRM Organization, Customer, Supplier and Employee, and a Frappe User for each person or agent with a " +
        "Seat.",
    },
    {
      label: "global-doctypes",
      text: "The directory itself holds Contact and CRM Organization rows with all their fields, shared by every tenant.",
    },
    { label: "own-shape", text: "Keep Capxul's own shape and map it only when a head is connected." },
  ],
  chosen: "identity-half",
  why:
    "The directory is global and holds nothing private (parties.directory-tenancy). Frappe's Contact and CRM " +
    "Organization are per-site records whose fields are what one business knows: a mailbox it was given, a phone, a " +
    "title, a territory, a revenue estimate. Global rows of them would show one tenant's knowledge to every tenant. " +
    "Split in two, the shape holds: the directory is what any counterparty may see and what makes a person or company " +
    "one across tenants, and each book holds the rest under Frappe's field names, so a head syncs by mapping. Frappe CRM " +
    "matches a person by mailbox only ('Match only on email which uniquely identifies a person', `contact_exists`), " +
    "which is the directory's key for a person, so a head's Contacts and every book's entries meet on the same Party. " +
    "Capxul's own shape, mapped only at a head, would leave an Organization without a head outside Frappe's shapes. The " +
    "Party's columns keep their names: a display name is a full name or an organization name by kind, and a Frappe " +
    "Contact without a last name is complete. A Party's name is identity, Capxul's alone (organizations.head-ownership): " +
    "what a head writes into a Contact's or CRM Organization's name is the owner's label, never the Party's " +
    "(contacts.head-mapping). This also settles core check C14: the directory leaks nothing a CRM keeps private.",
  source: crmBy("frappe/crm@2cecd300 crm/fcrm/doctype/crm_lead/crm_lead.py:335; frappe/frappe@1a7ea577 contacts/doctype/contact/contact.json; docs/vision/erp.md section 2, C14"),
  affects: [table_parties, procedure_parties_resolve_recipient, decision_parties_directory_tenancy, concept_parties, concept_contacts],
}

{
  id: "parties.head-parties",
  title: "A head's Customer, Supplier and Employee meet the directory by `capxul_party`",
  question:
    "A voucher's party is a directory Party id (books), a deal's or contact's is too (contacts), and a project's customer " +
    "is `customer_party_id` (projects). On a connected head these are ERPNext Customers, Suppliers and Employees. How " +
    "does a head document find its Party, what of one with none, and is every CRM customer a Party?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "custom-field",
      text:
        "Each of Contact, CRM Organization, Customer, Supplier and Employee carries the Party id in one Custom Field, " +
        "`capxul_party`, which only Capxul sets. When Capxul pushes a record naming a Party, the head's Capxul app finds " +
        "the document by that field, or creates it with the field set. A head document with no `capxul_party` (a customer " +
        "the head made, a supplier paid only by bank) is accepted with a null Party id: a head GL line against it comes " +
        "in with `party_id` null and the head's party name as its text. A head never names a company or an address and " +
        "never chooses a Safe; the one Party a head document can lead to is a person's, by mailbox, when an app's sync " +
        "takes in a document born there as a member would record it (a Contact's primary mailbox in contacts.head.sync, " +
        "an Employee's `personal_email` in payroll's, each through `parties.resolve-recipient`). A customer is a Party " +
        "only when it is one: a person by mailbox, an agent, an Organization on Capxul or an outside wallet; a company " +
        "not on Capxul is a private CRM entry with no Party (parties.outside-companies).",
    },
    { label: "match-by-name", text: "Match a head's Customer or Supplier to a Party by its name or email when it carries no Party." },
    { label: "name-from-head", text: "Name a new Party for every head Customer and Supplier." },
  ],
  chosen: "custom-field",
  why:
    "A Party is where money goes, so only Capxul binds one (organizations.head-ownership: identity is Capxul's). One " +
    "field name across the CRM, the books and payroll lets the Capxul app look up any document the same way, and it is " +
    "the name the CRM lane chose (payroll's `capxul_party_id` on Employee becomes `capxul_party`, " +
    "organizations.frappe-app-fields). Matching by name would let a head user choose whose Safe a voucher's party is; " +
    "naming Parties from a head would put a tenant's words in the global directory. A person named by mailbox carries " +
    "none: the mailbox fixes the Safe and the person later gives their own name, exactly as when a member records them " +
    "in Capxul (corrected in review: the first text said no Party is ever named from a head, which contacts' and " +
    "payroll's syncs contradict). A null Party keeps a head's own " +
    "bookkeeping whole without inventing identity. For projects this means `customer_party_id` is null for a customer " +
    "that is not on Capxul, so a project for a prospect company needs the CRM entry or the head's Customer name beside " +
    "it; projects sits below contacts and cannot read the entry, so that is the projects designer's to add.",
  source: asmBy("docs/design/frappe/accounting.md (capxul_party); docs/design/frappe/crm.md (Custom Fields); blueprint/projects/data.ts (customer_party_id)"),
  affects: [table_parties, component_frappe_app, concept_books, concept_contacts],
}

{
  id: "indexing.reorgs-are-ponders",
  title: "Ponder handles reorgs; finality is the reader's, through the indexer integration",
  question: "Who handles a chain reorganisation, and how does a reader know a fact will not be rolled back?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "ponders",
      text:
        "Ponder rolls back a reorganised block's rows and replays the canonical ones, so every view is the chain at " +
        "Ponder's head. A reader that books money reads at the deployment's finality depth (`indexer.factsOf`, " +
        "`awaitBlock`) and re-reads later where a fact could still go.",
    },
    { label: "finalized-only", text: "Ponder indexes only finalized blocks, so no view is ever rolled back." },
    { label: "app-retractions", text: "Capxul keeps its own checkpoints and a retraction protocol over Ponder's rows." },
  ],
  chosen: "ponders",
  why:
    "Ponder already owns canonical ordering, checkpoints and rollback, and the old indexer added no finality wait, " +
    "checkpoint or retraction protocol on top. Indexing only finalized blocks would hold every read (a hat just granted, " +
    "an approval's landing, the chain-settle budget of 3 s p95) behind finality, which on Base Sepolia is minutes. A " +
    "retraction protocol is the copy-and-correct the drift reconcile did, and it goes with it (concepts.indexing). So the " +
    "views show the head, and the readers that must not act on a fact that may vanish (payments settling, books booking, " +
    "a Movement's confirm step) wait for depth through the integration, which fails with a code while Ponder lags or " +
    "rebuilds. On a devnet Anvil mines at once and reorgs only when a test scripts one.",
  source: by("apps/indexer/CONTEXT.md:157 (Ponder owns rollback and replay); apps/indexer/README.md:4; P5 chain-settle"),
  affects: [...FACT_VIEWS, ...PROJECTIONS, table_indexer_progress, integration_indexer, component_ponder],
}

{
  id: "indexing.tables-only",
  title: "Indexing is tables only: no procedure, rpc, workflow, flow or operation",
  question:
    "Indexing owns every chain view and no workflow (concepts.indexing). Does it own any behaviour: read rpcs for other " +
    "concepts, the indexer service, a procedure, a flow?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "tables-only",
      text:
        "Indexing owns its views and nothing else. A concept that depends on indexing reads the views in its own rpcs and " +
        "workflows; what depends on Ponder's progress is the shared `indexer` integration; Ponder alone writes.",
    },
    {
      label: "read-rpcs",
      text: "Indexing exposes read rpcs (a Safe's transfers, a hat's wearers, a budget's tree) that other concepts call, like old `PonderService`.",
    },
    { label: "indexer-rpcs", text: "Indexing implements `head`, `awaitBlock` and `factsOf` as its own rpcs instead of an integration." },
  ],
  chosen: "tables-only",
  why:
    "One Postgres holds the views and every concept's tables, so a reader joins a view in its own transaction, under " +
    "row-level security, with no hop. A read rpc in indexing would be reached by no operation, flow, signal or trigger " +
    "(P2's unreached-rpc), and an rpc calling an rpc is not a step the book has. Ponder's progress is a call with a " +
    "timeout and a failure, not a read (integrations.indexer), and it serves every concept the same way, so it is the " +
    "shared integration. Nothing in `app` is indexing's to write and nothing writes Ponder's schema but Ponder " +
    "(components.ponder), so there is no procedure, and with no rpc there is nothing for a flow to compose. " +
    "OPERATION_OWNERS gives indexing no frozen operation (operations.owners): every command that shows a chain fact is " +
    "owned by the concept whose noun it shows.",
  source: by("packages/backend/src/integrations/ponder/service.ts:45 (old reader); P2; P8; blueprint/shared/foundation.ts (OPERATION_OWNERS)"),
  affects: [
    concept_indexing,
    integration_indexer,

{
  id: "agents.fde-authority",
  title: "The hosted FDE acts only as its asker, through the CLI; it never governs",
  question:

  options: [

        "It runs on Capxul's FDE host (aaron.fde-hosted), whose runtime holds its key, and acts only through the CLI and " +

        "(reading projects, working tasks and keeping its own time), adds or removes a Frappe app (`org head app add|remove`: a Director or the FDE, " +

        "allowance. It may never be a Director or wear the Shareholders' top hat, approve or execute a Board proposal, " +
        "sign the company Safe, change its own key, freeze, sweep or removal, raise or buy seats, pay its own hosting " +
        "(`org fde pay` needs a person), connect or disconnect a head, ask itself (`org fde ask` is a Director's), or sit " +
        "in another Organization.",
    },
    {
      label: "as-the-asker",
      text:
        "As seat-and-hats in what it never does, but under aaron.fde-anyone the hosted FDE acts only within a turn and " +
        "only as that turn's asker (organizations.fde-for-the-asker): every call it makes is the asker's, with their " +
        "Seat and hats, so it does for each asker exactly what they may do themselves, and for a guest only what a " +
        "counterparty may. It holds no authority of its own: it starts with no hat and needs none, and hats the Board " +
        "grants its Safe are not used while it is hosted. It never signs for anyone: an approval it prepares opens for " +
        "the asker's own Safe, which the asker signs. It never answers a preview for the asker (the head's connection, a " +

    "to answer. Every action is an ordinary command with its own trace, refusals and evals, the trace naming the FDE " +
    "and its asker, so nothing it does is invisible to the Organization. Hosted by Capxul, it is a runtime Capxul " +
    "operates for the Organization, which the Board can freeze, re-key or remove at any time; an app's add is the " +
    "Organization's choice, so it adds one only for a Director who asks.",

  affects: [table_agents, table_org_members, concept_organizations],
}

{
  id: "books.chart-tree",
  title: "The chart is ERPNext's Account tree; only ledger accounts take postings",
  question:
    "Capxul's chart had six types by a code's first digit and sub-accounts that could hold their own money. ERPNext's " +
    "chart is a tree of five root types in which only a ledger account takes GL Entries and an account with entries " +
    "cannot become a group. How does Capxul's chart sit in that tree without losing a frozen behaviour?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "tree-with-type-groups",
      text:
        "Five roots (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Income, Expenses) and two groups under Expenses (Cost of services, " +
        "Operating expenses) are Capxul's six types; they have no number and are not listed. A top-level account sits " +
        "directly under its type's group; a sub-account under a parent that becomes a group, which needs the parent to " +
        "hold no postings (else WRONG_STATE `parent_has_postings`) and to have no role and no Frappe account type (else " +
        "WRONG_STATE `parent_protected`). Codes keep Capxul's rule (first digit by type, unique " +
        "among active accounts, next in the parent's ten, next free hundred). Protected accounts fill the Company's " +
        "defaults by role, and each template account carries its Frappe account type.",
    },
    {
      label: "parents-hold-money",
      text:
        "Keep parents that hold money and translate at sync, giving each such parent a hidden ledger child in the head.",
    },
    { label: "erpnext-standard", text: "Adopt ERPNext's Standard chart with numbers (1000 assets … 5000 expenses), renumbering us-services." },
  ],
  chosen: "tree-with-type-groups",
  why:
    "Frappe refuses a GL Entry on a group and refuses to turn an account with entries into a group " +
    "(`validate_group_or_ledger`), so a parent that holds money has no honest Frappe shape: hidden children would be " +
    "accounts nobody made, with codes the unique number would have to invent. Renumbering to ERPNext's chart would " +
    "rewrite every claim that names 1010, 4999, 6999, 3990 or 6100. With type groups every frozen claim keeps its words: " +
    "add's 'a sub-account takes the next code under its parent and the parent's type' and 'a top-level account takes " +
    "the next free hundred in its range', the P&L's 'a sub-account's balance rolls into its parent's total, counted " +
    "once' (a group's total is its children's). One behaviour narrows that no claim covers: a sub-account can no longer " +

{

        "reclassifying a row posted on or before it is refused (WRONG_STATE `period_closed`; reclassify lists the row); the " +

{
  id: "banking.payout-books",
  title: "Banking's money sides carry their fee, log, Safe and Party; a payout its payee",
  question:
    "Books' vouchers need a rail's fee, the log index, the Safe and the counterparty's Party on every side, and a bank " +
    "payout's voucher needs the real payee, not Bridge's deposit address that the chain shows. Which does banking pass, " +
    "and how does a payout's reach books, since payments writes its fact?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "through-the-door",
      text:
        "The payout's item to `payments.prepare-command` carries `fee_raw` (the quote's `fee_amount`, in the token's " +
        "units) and, for a contact's account, `against` with the contact's Party as Supplier; payments keeps both on the " +
        "Payment from its birth and passes them at settlement. Banking's own facts (a deposit's credit, a payout's return) " +
        "carry the Safe, the Transfer's log index and the sender's Party when the directory has one; a deposit's " +
        "`fee_raw` is the gross less the net in the token's units when the token is the currency's own.",
    },
    { label: "annotate-later", text: "Leave the payout's fact unclassified and let a person or a head annotate it." },
  ],
  chosen: "through-the-door",
  why:
    "The payout and its Payment are one money fact (dependencies.payments-banking), so what the books post it against " +
    "is known at the quote and belongs on the Payment from its birth (payments.money-sides); a later annotation would " +
    "leave every payout in review. The fee is Bridge's number on the quote: neither payments nor books computes one. A " +
    "contact's account names its Party (`bank-accounts.party_id`), which Frappe makes a Supplier; a payout to your own " +
    "account (`self`) or to a payee known only by name has no party, and `bank pay --account` names a saved bank " +
    "account, not a ledger account, so no account is chosen: books posts the payout to its not-decided account with " +
    "the fee on bank charges until someone annotates it. A deposit's fee is only meaningful where the bank currency and " +
    "the token are one (USD and USDC, EUR and EURC); across a conversion the rate is Bridge's and the fee is left out. " +
    "The return references the payout's Payment (banking.payout-return-reference), so it nets against the same party " +
    "and account.",
  source: FRAPPE("docs/design/frappe/accounting.md (For other lanes: banking); blueprint/books/procedures.ts (MoneySide)"),
  affects: [

    workflow_banking_deposits_credit,

}

{
  id: "devnet.clock-rate",
  title: "A running clock has a rate, world seconds per real second, set by `dev time set`",
  question:
    "aaron.world-clock: a shared world may run faster than real time (every real hour moves its clock four), so the " +
    "clock gains a rate beside frozen and running. How is the rate set and changed, what bounds it, and what keeps it?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "rate",
      text:
        "The clock carries `rate`, the seconds of world time that pass in each real second while it runs: a whole number " +
        "from 1 to 60, 1 at `up` unless `capxul-devnet up --rate <n>`. The protocol sets it with `POST /v1/time/rate " +
        "{rate}` (devnet-control's timeRate); its CLI command is `dev time set --rate <n>` (operation dev.time.set, SDK " +
        "method devnet.time.set) and the supervisor's own client, which mirrors `dev time`'s verbs, is `capxul-devnet " +
        "time set --rate <n>`. A change takes effect " +
        "at once: the authority reads now at the change and sends a `rate` event (a new version, now, realAt and the " +
        "rate), so every follower runs on at the new rate from the same instant; nothing moves back and nothing is mined. " +
        "A real hour at rate r moves the world at most r hours, less the moments it stands at stops " +
        "(devnet.running-stops). It is a move: while a warp, step, settle, start-at, freeze or resume runs it is WRONG_STATE, " +
        "a race no saved world holds, so it is not a booked refusal, as the frozen `dev time` commands' is not. A frozen clock " +
        "keeps its rate for when it runs again; freeze, resume and every warp keep it; a saved world keeps its rate with " +
        "its now and mode, and a restore sets it; a season sets it when it starts (devnet.seasons). `dev time` shows it. " +
        "In a shared world only its owner sets it: a joiner's call is ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED (world shared-world-joiner). A rate " +
        "never changes a warp: a warp moves as far as it is told, at the barrier's pace.",
    },
    { label: "fast-mode", text: "A third mode, `fast`, beside frozen and running, at a fixed multiple." },
    { label: "timed-warps", text: "No standing rate: a program warps an hour every quarter of an hour." },
  ],
  chosen: "rate",
  why:
    "Aaron's ruling aaron.world-clock asks for a world whose clock moves four hours each real hour, beside the frozen " +
    "and running modes. A rate is the one number a running clock lacked: running at rate 1 is the running clock as it " +
    "was, so the modes stay two and every reader computes now one way. A fixed fast mode could not be four for one " +
    "world and ten for another; timed warps would jump, which is what the barrier replaced, and leave the head behind " +
    "between them. The bound protects what still runs on real time (time.real-elapsed): at 60 a Ponder poll of 100 ms " +
    "is six world seconds and a vendor's 2 s p95 two world minutes; past it the story stops reading as time passing, " +
    "and a faster story is a warp, which is a barrier. A rate also shortens in real time everything a person is " +
    "promised on now: at rate 4 a sign-in code's five minutes last 75 real seconds, so a world whose people sign in by " +
    "emailed codes runs at 5 or less. That is its owner's choice, not a refusal. For Aaron: the command (`dev time set " +
    "--rate <n>`, one operation beyond the 215 under rules.new-operations) and the bound of 60. The recommendation " +
    "stands until he answers.",
  source: WORLD_CLOCK("blueprint/shared/rulings.ts (aaron.world-clock); blueprint/access/decisions.ts (a code lasts five minutes); docs/design/new-commands.md (G3 `set`)"),
  affects: [
    flow_devnet_time_set, worldOps.operation_world_clock_set, flow_devnet_time_show, flow_devnet_time_resume, flow_devnet_time_freeze,
    flow_devnet_snapshots_save, flow_devnet_snapshots_restore, integration_devnet_control, component_devnet, environment_devnet,
    environment_shared_world,
  ],
}

{
  id: "devnet.follow-at-a-rate",
  title: "At a rate, a follower computes now from the event, capped at the next stop",
  question:
    "With a rate, a follower's now between events is the event's now plus the rate times the real time since. A " +
    "follower may also be on another machine (a shared world's real head, its FDE host), whose real clock is not the " +
    "authority's, and some followers are actors that think for real seconds. How does every follower compute one now, " +
    "never past a stop and never backward, and when does it acknowledge?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "capped-formula",
      text:
        "Every clock event and answer carries now, realAt, mode, rate and stopAt. Frozen, now is `now`. Running, now is " +
        "min(stopAt, now + rate × (t − realAt)), t being the follower's real time on the authority's real clock; a stop's " +
        "event has stopAt equal to now, so the clock stands. A follower on the authority's machine reads that clock. One " +
        "elsewhere measures its offset: every answer carries `realNow`, the authority's real time as it answered, and the " +
        "follower takes the offset from a `GET /v1/time` round trip at join and every minute, as NTP does; it never reads " +
        "a now earlier than one it read, holding at the last until the computed now passes it. A follower reports a due " +
        "instant earlier than its last as soon as it learns of it (`POST /v1/followers/<id>/due`), not only in an " +
        "acknowledgement. Machinery (the backend, Ponder, a head's jobs, the stand-ins) acknowledges a stop idle when its " +
        "work is done; an actor (a hosted FDE, a simulation's agent) acknowledges once it has taken the stop's work, not " +
        "when its thinking ends. A simulation that needs its agent's whole turn at one instant runs the clock frozen and " +
        "steps it, as vending-bench does.",
    },
    { label: "receipt", text: "Each follower times now from its own receipt of each event." },
  ],

{
  id: "devnet.followers",
  title: "Followers take the clock, report idle and their next due, and the barrier waits",
  question: "How does each component, and an outside program, follow the clock closely enough that a warp can wait for it?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "ack",
      text:
        "A follower joins under a name, takes every clock event, and acknowledges each version with whether it is idle " +
        "and its own next due instant (later than now, or none). The built-in followers are the backend (its devnet Now " +
        "layer: at each event it takes the new now and runs its timer and cron pump; it is idle when no due timer is " +
        "unfired; no workflow run or step is executing; the engine's message storage holds nothing deliverable that " +
        "has not been processed (a resume, a deferred's completion, a new execution, a run's retry); its outbox is " +
        "delivered; and its wake router has consumed every row up to the block Ponder has indexed), Ponder (through " +
        "the supervisor: idle when its indexed block is the head), the bundler stand-in (idle when its mempool is empty " +
        "and no bundle is in flight), the paymaster stand-in, the Bridge stand-in (its scheduled answers are its next " +
        "due), each stand-in Frappe head (idle when no ring it sent is unanswered, with no next due: " +
        "devnet.head-stand-in) and the stand-in WhatsApp (idle once every webhook it posted is answered, its earliest " +
        "redelivery its next due: devnet.whatsapp-stand-in). An armed fault switch's held state counts as idle (a held receipt, an indexer hold). An outside program " +
        "joins the same way, so a simulation's own happenings become stops. Running, a follower computes now from the " +
        "event's now, realAt, rate and next stop (devnet.follow-at-a-rate). A follower that misses an " +
        "acknowledgement fails the barrier and is dropped. The backend's follower channel is the runtime's, not an rpc. " +
        "A follower that keeps world state outside the chain and Postgres (a real bench, the world's FDE namespace) joins " +
        "stateful, and saves and restores that state with every world (devnet.stateful-followers).",
    },

  ],
  chosen: "ack",
  why:
    "A barrier needs to know that each part has taken the new time and finished what fell due, which only the part can " +
    "say; next due lets the warp stop where something happens instead of at every second. Reading the supervisor on " +
    "every use puts a round trip in every rpc. The backend's follower is runtime plumbing like the outbox relay " +
    "(rules.outbox): booking it as an rpc only the supervisor calls would be unreached (P2). Using the public protocol " +
    "for the built-in followers keeps one path, proven by Capxul's own use. 'No step running and the outbox delivered' " +

    "the run begins (Effect's cluster persists the message and only then reads it), and in the gap after Ponder " +

    "come. A follower that timed now from its own receipt of an event would trail the authority by the event's " +

  affects: [flow_devnet_time_follow, flow_devnet_time_settle, integration_devnet_control, component_devnet, environment_devnet],
}

{
  id: "devnet.mine-to-depth",
  title: "A stop mines empty blocks until its last transaction is twice the finality depth",
  question:
    "The supervisor mines only when something is pending, so no block follows a quiet one. Readers that wait for a fact " +

      label: "mine-to-depth",

        "until the newest block that carries a transaction is 2k deep, the depth of payments' confirm read; with k = 0 " +
        "it mines none. The blocks are part of the stop's settle rounds, so every depth wait ends inside the stop that " +
        "mined its fact. A scripted reorg (`capxul-devnet chain`) replaces blocks within that depth, as on staging.",
    },
    { label: "zero", text: "Set the devnet's finality depth to 0, so a fact is final in the block that mined it." },

    "year, each one Ponder must index. Mining to depth inside the stop costs 2k empty blocks per stop that carried a " +

{
  id: "devnet.only-miner",
  title: "The supervisor is the chain's only miner, and every block is mined at now",
  question: "Anvil keeps its own clock, which runs with the wall between blocks and mines a block per transaction. How is a block's time made the devnet's now?",
  options: [
    {
      label: "only-miner",
      text:
        "Anvil runs with automine off. The supervisor watches its pending transactions and mines each batch at once with " +
        "evm_mine at now (to the second), and pins Anvil's own time to now at every clock change, so an eth_call or a gas " +
        "estimate at `pending` sees now as block.timestamp. On a frozen clock every move ends with the head at now: a " +
        "stop of a warp or step, a start-at, a freeze that moved now and a restore each end by mining an empty block at " +
        "now when nothing else was mined at that second, so `latest` reads now and chain-rpc reads at `latest` on every " +
        "environment, with no devnet branch. A stop opens with the head at its second: when the head is earlier, the " +
        "authority mines an empty block at the stop's instant before it sends the stop event, so a timer for a deadline " +
        "the chain enforces finds the head at its due second (time.chain-judged-deadlines) and waits inside the stop only " +
        "for Ponder; a running clock's stops do the same (devnet.running-stops). A stop's cascade (a timer's transaction, then the one its indexed fact " +
        "wakes, then the empty blocks of devnet.mine-to-depth) mines several blocks in one second, which the pinned " +
        "Anvil must accept (B0 measures it). If it does not, the authority ticks now forward one second before such a " +
        "block (a `tick` event to every follower), which keeps time forward but carries a stop's later work past its " +
        "instant: the warp's due instants (time.due-fires-once) and a frozen story's repeatability " +
        "(time.frozen-deterministic) then hold only for stops that mine once, and B3 records how mining is made " +
        "deterministic before anything relies on them.",
    },
    { label: "automine", text: "Keep automine and set Anvil's time before each warp, letting it run with the wall in between." },
  ],
  chosen: "only-miner",
  why:
    "With automine, every transaction's block takes Anvil's own clock, which moves with the wall: on a frozen devnet a " +
    "day-old story would mine at today's time, and a payment's block time would disagree with the backend's row. Mining " +
    "on demand costs a millisecond or two over automine and batches concurrent transactions as a real chain does. A " +
    "head left behind now after a stop that mined nothing would make every contract view that computes from " +
    "block.timestamp read the past at `latest` (Agreements' released pay, Budgets' period, Governor.state), and reading " +
    "at `pending` only on a devnet is a branch staging never runs. The tick cannot be the quiet fallback it looked: how " +
    "many ticks a stop takes depends on how its transactions happen to batch, which is timing, not the story. Revised " +
    "by the time review, 8 November 2026. Revised again by the world-clock pass, 8 November 2026: a stop that mined its " +
    "head block only at its end left a chain-judged timer, which fires as the stop opens, a block short of its second, " +
    "so it re-armed past its own instant; on a quiet running devnet nothing mined at all, so it re-armed for ever.",
  source: TIME(`${OLD_WORLD}/README.md (Anvil's clock moves with the wall); ${OLD_WORLD}/service.ts:240-270, :493`),
  affects: [component_devnet, environment_devnet, integration_chain_rpc, flow_devnet_time_warp, flow_devnet_time_start_at, flow_devnet_time_step],
}
